correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and finite boundaries are fixed explicitly. The forest independence criterion is a bijective change of coordinates from independent vertex permutations to root and edge permutations. The converse uses an exact (n!)^{c-k} equality-conjunction count. The mixed cumulant is derived by complete three-type partition of directed-edge triples, with exact compatibility counts and rational simplification. Strict positivity holds for \(n\ge2\). An embedded standalone checker exhaustively enumerates all triples of full orders for n<=4, independent compatible-edge counts through n<=8, and relative-permutation distributions on small trees and triangles; finite checks corroborate rather than replace the general proof.

evidence: Bender and Canfield, Theorem 1, gives asymptotic Poisson probabilities for the number of edges common simultaneously to t random sparse-graph embeddings.
Jeż et al., Theorem 1.1, concerns finite satisfiability of FO² with arbitrarily many successors in 2EXPSPACE, not random model distributions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither cited theorem implies the exact graph-indexed mutual independence of all pair-local FO² tests nor the finite-n three-pair cumulant. An all-common-edge statistic is not the triangular interaction of three different pairwise intersections.

A general tree-edge group-coordinate bijection explains the forest part; this known mechanism is explicitly credited.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus semantic searches for forest-index independence, the exact triangular directed-overlap cumulant, and equivalent formulations were compared with primary articles. The closest exact triangle-cumulant index result concerns LKJ correlation matrices rather than successor paths, while the older shared-adjacency paper gives a two-order marginal only, and the sparse-graph theorem addresses edges common to all samples asymptotically. The 2026 motivating article studies decidability, not probabilistic model independence. The elementary group-difference mechanism itself is credited and not asserted new; the application and exact natural triangular cumulant remain unmatched in inspected coverage. Residual unlocated general exchangeable-statistics results remain a risk.
residual_risks: Historical general group-valued random edge-difference independence may subsume the forest criterion; the general mechanism is not claimed original.
Broader permutation-statistics literature could contain the exact three-way overlap moment under other terminology.
The older Bender–Canfield PDF visual screenshot was unavailable; inspected extracted statements are clear but not a complete visual full-text examination.

value.rationale: The graph-indexed forest/cycle boundary completely classifies when *every* pair-successor FO² sentence family has independent truth values under the natural uniform finite-model measure. Cycles admit explicit definable dependence with exact finite-n joint probabilities. The first nontrivial natural overlap interaction is quantified by a positive sharp \(1/n\) mixed third cumulant, distinguishing pairwise independence from genuine independence. These are structural and quantitative properties of the exact multi-successor model class, not arbitrary parameter slices or a recomputation of the known two-order marginal.
